                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> During the mobility, your institution fosters the integration of the incoming mobile participants</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The institution appoints responsible person(s) to deal with practical issues (e.g. social, health, and/or psychological problems)</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The institution should ensure there are named, visible persons who are responsible for the practical issues associated with integrating mobile students. This visibility should be ensured through introduction to this function during the Welcome / Orientation period and be detailed on the website so all mobile students can easily access this support, throughout their stay.&nbsp;</p><p>Non-academic mentoring and support arrangements should already be outlined in the Course Catalogue of the receiving HEI, in the section on general information for students, with relevant contact persons in the respective areas. Academic advisors should have close contact with the practical services which are available to incoming participants as they are often the first line of contact to the incoming student. Further information sessions should be arranged for all staff who work with incoming students to ensure they are adequately signposted on to the appropriate services they require.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It appoints responsible person(s) to deal with academic issues (course timetables, student attendance, coursework, relationship with academic staff, etc.)</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is important that the receiving institution appoints specific named academic advisors who are responsible for dealing with problems related to academic issues (course timetables, student attendance, coursework, relationship with academic staff, etc.) of incoming students.&nbsp; Information on mentoring for thesis writing for incoming students is particularly important and clear mentoring arrangements should be agreed upon between the student, sending and receiving institutions and organised before the mobility.</p><p>For traineeships, a mentor, different from the supervisor, should be nominated to support and encourage the mobile student while in the receiving organisation. The mentor should also provide information on the culture of the enterprise and informal codes and conducts, of the receiving organisation. The contact details of both the supervisor and the mentor should be specified in the Learning Agreement.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It organises Welcome / Orientation activities at the beginning of each semester</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>An important aspect of the support arrangement is the welcome or orientation activities. These welcome / orientation activities should provide the incoming students with the necessary information on practical and administrative arrangements, to allow incoming students to meet local and other mobile students, to introduce the learning and teaching methods of the receiving institution, academic regulations, the institutional culture, health and safety issues. These activities should address any type of concern of the incoming student, and reduce any psychological pressure they might feel during their first contacts at the receiving institution. The welcome&nbsp; / orientation activities should be designed to take into account any cultural and religious sensitivities of the incoming students (ensuring a range of activities to suit different types of students).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It organises activities to integrate them in the receiving institution and the local community, e.g. with the support of student organisations, Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association etc.</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>As well as academic and practical support from the institution, incoming students need to feel fully integrated into the student community, something which is best done by their fellow students / peers. Local student association(s), such as Erasmus Student Network (ESN) and the other associations’ member of the ESAA - Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association (<a href="http://esaa-eu.org/">http://esaa-eu.org/</a>), play an important role in supporting incoming students. Incoming students need to feel welcomed and included in the student organisations. To help this process, the student organisations need to be aware of their role in supporting this integration and have access to the right resources, information, guidance and incentives. As institutions often have many types of student organisations, cooperation between them is encouraged through meetings together, social activities and buddy programmes. A key aspect of these activities is to make sure they are for all students so incoming students are integrated with the local students and hence the culture. Student organisations include for example, ESN (Erasmus Student Network) or ESAA - Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association (<a href="http://esaa-eu.org/">http://esaa-eu.org/</a>). ESAA runs a buddy system to encourage integration of incoming students with their peers inside the institution and share good practice with other member associations around Europe.</p>                      </div>

                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> At the end of the mobility, your institution has formal procedures for recognising student mobility (good practices linked to recognition at the end of the mobility, e.g. in the use of Transcripts of Records and Grade Distribution Tables)</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records are issued in a timely manner (normally 5 weeks) to both incoming and outgoing students</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important in the recognition framework to provide Transcripts of Records in a timely manner, immediately following the mobility period. After the mobility, the receiving institution should send a Transcript of Records to the student and to the sending institution within a period stipulated in the Inter-Institutional Agreement (normally within five weeks after publication/proclamation of the student’s results at the receiving institution). It can be provided electronically or through any other means accessible to the student and the sending institution. The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should refer to the educational components agreed upon in the Learning Agreement. Grade distribution information should be included as well, either as a web link or an annex.</p><p>Following the receipt of the Transcript of Records from the receiving institution, the sending institution should automatically transfer and recognise the student’s academic outcomes successfully completed at the receiving institution, as agreed in the Learning Agreement, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The Sending Institution will provide a Transcript of Records to the student or record the results in a database or any other means accessible to the student, normally within five weeks after having received the transcript of the receiving institution. The EU official template for the Learning Agreement for studies (including the Transcript of Records) is available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm</a></p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">All credits gained by students during a period of study abroad that were specified in the final version of the Learning Agreement are automatically transferred by your institution and count towards the students' final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The sending institution should ensure that all the credits earned by the mobile student during the mobility period are recognised and counted towards the final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The period of study abroad must be clear in the student's records and documents issued to the student (Diploma Supplement or equivalent). This is a golden rule of recognition of credit mobility within the framework of inter-institutional agreements. All the credits towards the student's degree that are earned during the mobility period and which were originally agreed on in the Learning Agreement (or a revised version to it) should be recognised by the sending HEI without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. Learning Agreements are binding for all the parties and require that, on successful completion of the mobility period, the sending HEI recognises credits earned by the student and documents these credits in the student records, so they can be identified in a transparent way.</p><p>Upon receipt of the Transcript of Records or Training Certificates, the sending HEI should:<br>a) certify the mobile student has fulfilled all requirements stipulated in the Learning Agreement;<br>b) ensure recognition of the mobility period abroad within the time-scale and according to the conditions stipulated in the institutional recognition framework.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records of incoming students include a description of or a link to the national grading system</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should include grade distribution information, either as a web link or an annex. The local grading scale should be clearly explained, with a statistical distribution of local grades, to provide transparency and understanding of grading practices at the host institution. Where applicable, use should be made of a Grade Distribution Table for the programme of study, according to the ECTS Users’ Guide (<a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm</a>).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility. There are more details on this in the ECTS Users’ Guide.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">In addition to recognising formal learning, the institution recognises any non-formal or informal learning acquired during the mobility according to the ECTS Users’ Guide, e.g. by awarding ECTS credits for volunteering</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>During a period of mobility, students often take advantage of other opportunities outside of their required courses. These may include specific activities which can be considered non-formal or informal learning where they have acquired new skills. This could include additional language and cultural courses, extra-curricular activities, setting up a business and volunteer work undertaken by the student in that period or upon return at the receiving institution.</p>                      </div>

                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution issues a Diploma Supplement</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>

                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">To all students, automatically, free of charge and in a major European language</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>This Supplement should include a record of the period of mobility under the Erasmus+ Programme. The 48 European countries taking part in the Bologna Process have agreed that each mobile graduate in their respective country should receive the Diploma Supplement (DS) automatically, free of charge and in at least one of the major European languages in addition to the national language. The HEI should issue a Diploma Supplement (or equivalent) to accompany every degree successfully completed by a student, using - where applicable - the template developed by the European Commission, the Council of Europe and UNESCO. The HEI's policy on issuing the Diploma Supplement should be published on its website.</p><p>The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm&nbsp;</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">That includes a record of the mobility period(s) carried out by the student under the Erasmus+ programme</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The information contained in the Transcript of Records from the Receiving Institution should also be included in the Diploma Supplement produced by the Sending Institution (at least for Sending Institutions located in Programme Countries), with the exact titles of the components that the student has followed abroad. Alongside modules or units taken at the sending HEI, the Diploma Supplement should list recognised modules, units and/or training activities undertaken during the student's mobility period and indicate the location of these mobility activities.<br>In the case of double, multiple or joint degrees, the Diploma Supplement should indicate the name and status of the partner HEIs awarding the degree and explain the respective language(s) of instruction and examination. In addition, an explanation should be provided about the grading and classification scheme agreed by the awarding HEIs. The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm</a>&nbsp;</p>                      </div>

                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">13</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-mobility-supporting-individuals-development-and-institutional-aims-and-objectives" target="_blank">Recognition of staff mobility – supporting individuals’ development and institutional aims and objectives</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-participating-in-erasmus-staff-mobility-actions-and-international-cooperation-projects" target="_blank">Recognition of staff participating in Erasmus staff mobility actions and international cooperation projects</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/capitalising-on-the-outcomes-and-experiences-of-erasmus-activities" target="_blank">Capitalising on the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-erasmus-impact-study-effects-of-mobility-on-the-skills-and-employability-of-students-and-the-internationalisation-of-higher-education-institutions" target="_blank">The Erasmus Impact Study: Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>

</div>

Moderne Infrastruktur

Du willst nicht nur bestehende Infrastruktur verwalten, sondern moderne DevOps- und Cloud-Umgebungen aktiv aufbauen und kontinuierlich weiterentwickeln? Für unseren Partner im FInance-Umfeld in Frankfurt am Main suchen wir erfahrene DevOps Engineers / Senior DevOps Engineers (m/w/d), die moderne Entwicklungs- und Betriebsprozesse ganzheitlich gestalten – von CI/CD und Infrastructure as Code über Containerisierung und Kubernetes bis hin zu hochautomatisierten Cloud- und On-Premise-Plattformen.

Die Position verfolgt einen konsequenten Platform-First-Ansatz: Entwicklungs- und Betriebsprozesse werden end-to-end analysiert, standardisiert und automatisiert und tief in bestehende Entwicklungs-, IT- und Geschäftsabläufe integriert – in regulierten, sicherheitskritischen Umfeldern mit hohem Gestaltungsspielraum.

Aufgaben

  • DevOps- und Plattformlösungen konzipieren und umsetzen
  • CI/CD-Pipelines entwickeln und optimieren
  • Infrastructure as Code etablieren
  • Container- und Kubernetes-Umgebungen aufbauen und betreiben
  • Cloud- und On-Premise-Infrastrukturen integrieren
  • GitOps und automatisierte Betriebsprozesse etablieren und weiterentwickeln
  • Monitoring, Logging und Observability aufbauen und verbessern
  • Security und Compliance in den DevOps-Prozess integrieren
  • Entwicklungs- und Betriebsprozesse kontinuierlich verbessern

Qualifikation

  • Mehrjährige, belegbare Praxiserfahrung im DevOps-, Cloud- oder Platform-Engineering
  • Erfahrung mit CI/CD, Git, Infrastructure as Code und automatisierten Deployment-Prozessen
  • Sicherer Umgang mit Linux
  • Praktische Erfahrung mit Docker und Kubernetes
  • Erfahrung mit Cloud-Plattformen
  • Kenntnisse in Technologien wie Terraform, Ansible, GitLab CI/CD, Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions oder vergleichbaren Tools
  • Erfahrung mit GitOps, Monitoring, Logging und Observability von Vorteil
  • Verständnis für moderne Softwareentwicklungsprozesse und die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Development und Operations
  • Erfahrung im Aufbau und Betrieb produktiver, hochverfügbarer und skalierbarer Systeme
  • Ausgeprägte Hands-on-Mentalität
  • Erfahrung in regulierten oder sicherheitskritischen Umfeldern (z. B. Finanz- oder Versicherungsbranche) von Vorteil
  • Sehr gute (mind. C1) Deutsch- und gute bis sehr gute Englischkenntnisse

Benefits

  • Gehalt zwischen 75.000 € und 100.000 € je nach Erfahrung
  • Technologisch anspruchsvolles Umfeld mit viel Gestaltungsspielraum beim Aufbau moderner DevOps- und Plattform-Ansätze
  • Arbeit an der Schnittstelle von Entwicklung, Infrastruktur und Cloud – mit echter Verantwortung für produktive Systeme
  • Fokus auf Automation, Infrastructure as Code und moderne Engineering-Praktiken statt manueller Administration
  • Arbeit mit modernen Cloud-, Container- und Orchestrierungstechnologie

    You can watch the Meet the engineering team video to get a feeling for how we work.

    The role

    Platform Engineers own the shared capabilities that Langdock's products are built on. They treat these capabilities as internal products: defining the interfaces other teams build against and remaining accountable for their reliability, evolution, and operation over time.

    The work is to turn complex capabilities such as model access, agent execution, authorization, queues, integrations, document processing, and sandboxed compute into stable, reusable building blocks. Each capability needs a clear contract and must be able to evolve without forcing coordinated changes across the rest of the product.

    You own a service from design through long-term operation. That includes defining its API and failure behavior, planning migrations, implementing and deploying it, making it observable, and responding when it fails in production. When a service requires a new underlying mechanism, you work with Systems Engineers while remaining accountable for the service boundary and lifecycle.

    What you might work on

    Current platform work includes:

    • A durable agent runtime. The current engine runs model and tool loops for Chat, Workflows, automations, and subagents, but active execution is still owned by one process. We are separating the runtime from product-specific state and designing durable runs that can wait for approvals or external events, recover after a process dies, and continue without repeating committed tool calls. This also includes deterministic context reconstruction, compaction, and prompt-cache efficiency.

    • The Model Gateway. We are building one inference boundary for every Langdock product, with a model-agnostic API over managed and customer-provided models. The work includes provider adapters, routing across accounts and regions, rate limits, bounded fallback, streaming safety, usage tracking, and a control plane.

    • Shared services with explicit contracts. We are moving selected capabilities out of a TypeScript monolith into independently operated services with Protobuf and gRPC contracts inside one Bazel monorepo. Our authorization service, written in Go with embedded SpiceDB, is one example: the migration uses an outbox, shadow comparisons on production traffic, and consistency tokens before it becomes authoritative.

    • The integration and tool platform. Langdock already connects to external services through REST APIs, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and agent-to-agent (A2A) communication. The platform work is to make authentication, token refresh, rate limits, approvals, outbound network safety, and tool execution consistent across these paths.

    • Code execution as a shared service. Langdock already runs untrusted JavaScript, Bash, and Python through separate execution environments. Platform work includes defining a consistent execution API, lifecycle, permission model, resource budgets, and operational boundary, while partnering with Systems Engineers on the underlying isolation and scheduling mechanisms.

    • Production confidence for shared systems. Platform changes need evidence before rollout. Current work includes a reusable load-testing system for HTTP, gRPC, and streaming workloads; structured logging without user content or personally identifiable information (PII); and online database changes for PostgreSQL tables measured in hundreds of gigabytes or terabytes.

    • Storage and data systems. Improve how large volumes of customer and agent-generated data are stored, versioned, moved, and recovered while preserving consistency, data residency, and predictable performance.

    About Relation

    Relation is a sector defining TechBio company developing transformational medicines, with technology at our core. Our ambition is to understand human biology in unprecedented ways, discovering therapies to treat some of life’s most devastating diseases. We leverage single-cell multi-omics from patient tissue, functional assays, and machine learning to drive disease understanding, from cause to cure.

    We are scaling rapidly and building a team of exceptional individuals to push the boundaries of drug discovery. You will work in highly interdisciplinary teams where biology, computation, and engineering come together to solve complex problems that have not been solved before. Our state-of-the-art wet and dry labs in the heart of London are designed to accelerate this integration and translate insight into impact.

    We are committed to building diverse and inclusive teams. Relation is an equal opportunities employer and does not discriminate on the basis of gender, sexual orientation, marital or civil partnership status, gender reassignment, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief, disability, or age.

    By joining Relation, you will help define how medicines are discovered and deliver meaningful impact for patients.

    The opportunity

    Relation is offering a unique opportunity for an experienced Associate Director in Alliance Management to ensure that our strategic pharma partnerships continue to thrive and deliver. Working across high-profile collaborations including GSK and Novartis, you will be the connective tissue between Relation and our partners - building trusted relationships, creating clarity across complex collaborations and helping both organisations work together effectively towards shared strategic goals.

    You will sit at the centre of Relation’s partnership model, working closely with Programme Leaders, interdisciplinary teams and senior leaders across Relation and our partner organisations. You will have a highly visible role to safeguard relationship health, contractual alignment and forward visibility - ensuring that the right conversations happen at the right time, commitments are clearly understood, risks and opportunities are surfaced early, and that governance enables high-quality decision making at pace.

    You will bring together different perspectives with clarity and pragmatism, helping our partnerships operate as one team, while ensuring commitment to Relation’s high scientific standards, platform integrity and strategic priorities. The delivery of successful partnerships strengthen both partner organisations, and ultimately help to fulfill Relation’s goal of bringing transformational medicines to patients.

    Day to day you will:

    • Manage the health and effectiveness of strategic pharma partnerships, building trusted relationships across Relation and partner organisations and influencing cross-functional stakeholders at all levels to maintain alignment and momentum.

    • Shape and steward partnership governance, ensuring governance meetings focus on the decisions, risks and opportunities that matter, with clear ownership, effective escalation and disciplined follow-through.

    • Maintain forward visibility across each alliance, anticipating relational, contractual and governance risks and opportunities and ensuring they are surfaced early to the appropriate decision-makers.

    • Safeguard contractual alignment, maintaining oversight of scope, milestones, reporting requirements, financial triggers, data-sharing commitments and other obligations; translating contractual terms into clear implications for teams and governance.

    • Influence across organisational boundaries, connecting Programme Leaders, interdisciplinary teams, senior leadership and partner stakeholders to resolve ambiguity, navigate competing perspectives and enable timely decisions.

    • Lead alliance-level escalation, bringing clarity to complex or sensitive issues and ensuring escalation strengthens decision-making.

    • Shape new partnerships from diligence through launch, collaborating closely with Growth, Corporate and Business Development to embed effective governance, contractual clarity and practical ways of working from the outset.

    • Raise the standard of partnering at Relation, applying learning across collaborations to strengthen governance, alliance management and organisational partnering capability as Relation’s portfolio grows.

    Professionally, you will have:

    • A university degree in a relevant scientific or technical field, or equivalent experience.

    • Significant experience in alliance management or strategic partnerships within biotech or pharmaceutical R&D, including substantial experience working with large pharmaceutical partners.

    • Deep expertise working with complex collaboration agreements, with the judgement to interpret contractual commitments, identify implications and risks, and translate them into clear actions or governance decisions.

    We’re looking for a Product Strategy Analyst

    You'll shape how new businesses become iwoca customers – the sign-up flow, the documents we ask for, and the models that decide who gets funded and on what terms.

    Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

    The team

    The New Customers team owns everything from a business's first application to a funded loan: the application flow, the logic that routes each application, the documents we ask customers for, and the models that set loan amounts and pricing.

    The team is cross-functional – data scientists, analysts, and software engineers – and sets its own goals and direction. It partners closely with credit risk on the trade-offs behind every lending decision. Knowledge sharing is central to how the team works, supported by regular forums to share findings, and dedicated research and development time.

    The role

    • Judgement and strategy. You'll set iwoca's new-customer lending strategy, weighing trade-offs between speed, friction, risk, and decision accuracy. You'll identify drop-off points and commercial opportunities across the conversion funnel, and propose the initiatives that address them.

    • Challenge and experimentation. You'll design, run, and interpret controlled experiments on changes to the customer journey and new loan features. You'll apply statistical thinking so decisions rest on evidence.

    • Autonomy and growth. You'll manage analytical and strategic projects end-to-end, sharing findings and recommendations directly with senior leadership. You'll partner with the Team Lead to shape the team's long-term roadmap, with the expectation of growing into a Team Lead role yourself.

    • Commercial analytics. You've worked in strategy, analytics, product, finance, or consulting. You understand how to use data to make commercial decisions on revenue, cost, or risk that the business acts on.

    • Quantitative foundations. You have a STEM background (degree or equivalent) in mathematics, statistics, physics, engineering, or similar. You reason about uncertainty and calibration, grounded in the underlying statistics.

    • First-principles thinking. You break complex problems into their core parts, decide which to tackle first, and iterate systematically to a solution.

    • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

    • Customer journey analytics. You have analysed and improved a customer journey, balancing conversion, risk, and long-term value.

    • Coding abilities. You can code for analysis, automation, or prototypes - whether directly or via AI coding tools like Claude Code.

    Venez rejoindre l'IMT Mines Alès, grande école de prestige qui se classe parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs sur le plan national et mondial et implantée à Alès, ville à taille humaine, capitale des Cévennes où la qualité de vie est fortement appréciée par ses habitants.

    Créée en 1843, IMT Mines Alès compte à ce jour 1400 élèves (dont 250 étrangers) et 380 personnels. L’école dispose de 3 centres de recherche et d’enseignement de haut niveau scientifique et technologique, qui œuvrent dans les domaines des matériaux et du génie civil (C2MA), de l’environnement et des risques (CREER), de l’intelligence artificielle et du génie industriel et numérique (CERIS).     Vous êtes rattaché(e) au Centre de Recherche et d’Enseignement en Environnement et Risques (CREER) de l'IMT Mines Alès et dans l'unité de recherche : HSM.

    Ce travail s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet PREV’IA qui s’intéresse à la connaissance et à la prévision des ressources en eaux de la nappe plioquaternaire de la plaine de Roussillon, et de la source du Lez qui alimente Montpellier en eau potable.

    Votre travail s’inscrira dans la continuité d’une thèse en cours au sein de l’UMR HSM (équipe HYTAKE), portant sur la durabilité de la ressource en eau karstique (aquifère du Lez) alimentant une métropole méditerranéenne (Montpellier) en contexte de changement climatique.

     

    Votre mission :

    • Utiliser les concepts émergeants dans les approches de « Physics Informed Machine Learning » (PIML) pour évaluer les intérêts d’une synergie en modélisation hydrogéologique : (1) à base conceptuelle d’une part et (2) à base de réseaux de neurones informés, ou complémentés, par la physique. L’approche PIML (Physics Informed Machine Learning) est développée, avec deux courants : (i) les Physics Informed Architecture (PIA) : intégration de connaissances physiques dans l’architecture du modèle (couches cachées) ; et (ii) les Physics Informed Loss Function (PILF) : combinaison de modélisations physiques (équations différentielles) et boîte noire, fusionnées dans la fonction de coût (terme de régularisation). Les deux méthodes pourront être explorées. Les modèles proposés pourront être utilisés pour déterminer l’évolution de certaines grandeurs hydrologiques en réponse au changement climatique.

      Your wellbeing, our mission. Join a company shaping a healthier world.

      GET TO KNOW US

      At Wellhub we're revolutionizing workplace wellness. Our platform connects employees worldwide to the best partners for fitness, mindfulness, therapy, nutrition, and sleep—all in one simple subscription. Headquartered in NYC with team members in Europe, North America and South America, we're on a mission to make every company a wellness company.We believe work should be fulfilling, inspiring, and balanced. Here, you'll find a team that values wellbeing, collaboration, and different perspectives, where passion and creativity push boundaries to create real impact. Your contributions will help shape a healthier, more balanced world for you and millions of people globally. 

      Join us in redefining the future of wellbeing!

      THE OPPORTUNITY

      Partner Marketing exists to fuel the growth and success of Wellhub's global partner network of gyms, studios and wellness businesses. The Senior Manager, Partner Marketing (France & Benelux) leads Partner Marketing strategy and execution for these markets, as part of Wellhub's regional EU Partner Marketing team.

      This person will act as the regional Point of Contact (POC) for Partner Marketing in France and Benelux, owning the local Business-to- Partner value proposition, brand positioning, network growth and engagement and, fitness industry events, working closely with Partnerships, local and cross-functional Marketing, Wellbeing Engagement, Product Development and Revenue teams to align strategy and execution. Reporting to the Partner Marketing Director, EU, this role combines strategic ownership of the region with hands-on execution.

      This role directly impacts the growth and satisfaction of Wellhub's partner network in France and Benelux, contributing to the team's broader goals around partner network growth, partner engagement, and partner satisfaction (PSAT).

       

      YOUR IMPACT

      • Market-Specific Value Proposition: Develop and implement the local Business to Partner value proposition across all partner-facing materials and touchpoints for France and Benelux.
      • Brand Awareness & Positioning: Build Wellhub's presence and credibility within the regional fitness industry through relationships with industry associations/alliances, sponsorships, events, media/publications, and key opinion leaders (KOLs).
      • Strategic Partner Growth (B2P2C): Lead go-to-market strategy for partner launches, relaunches, and dedicated campaigns and promotions to end users and clients, driving growth with existing partners.
      • Strategic Partner Engagement: Build partner trust through structured engagement initiatives, including fitness industry events, partner conferences and summits.
      • Network Growth Support: Support the Demand Generation team's strategy with local market insights and develop sales enablement materials to drive growth across the partner network.
      • Cross-Functional Alignment: Partner closely with Partnerships,  User Growth, Corporate communication, Content, Revenue teams local and global level to align initiatives with company-wide strategy.
      • Budget Ownership: Manage the regional Partner Marketing budget for France and Benelux, allocating resources across campaigns, events and other marketing initiatives to drive results and maximize ROI.
      • Data-Driven Marketing: Use performance data and partner insights to inform, prioritize and continuously optimize Partner Marketing initiatives in the region.
      • AI-Driven Productivity: Autonomously identify and apply AI tools (e.g., Gemini, Claude) to raise the team's level of automation — streamlining repetitive tasks, accelerating content, reporting and campaign production, and embedding AI-assisted workflows into day-to-day ways of working. Continuously build personal AI fluency and share practices that help the broader team work smarter.
      • Live the mission: inspire and empower others by genuinely caring for your own wellbeing and your colleagues. Bring wellbeing to the forefront of work, and create a supportive environment where everyone feels comfortable taking care of themselves, taking time off, and finding work-life wellness.

      WHO YOU ARE

      • Native/fluent in French and fluent in English, based in France with deep knowledge of local market and fitness industry culture.
      • Working knowledge of Dutch is a plus, given the scope across Benelux markets.
      • [+8] years of experience in Marketing, ideally with exposure to Partner, Channel, Product or Revenue Marketing in a B2B or B2B2C environment.
      • Proven ability to build value propositions, brand positioning and go-to-market strategies, and to execute them independently as a regional lead.
      • Comfortable managing institutional relationships with industry KOLs, associations and strategic partners.
      • Strong cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder management skills.
      • Data-driven approach to marketing decisions, comfortable with CRM and marketing analytics tools.
      • Fluent English is mandatory.

      We recognize that individuals approach job applications differently. We strongly encourage all aspiring applicants to go for it, even if they don't match the job description 100%. We welcome your application and will be delighted to explore if you could be a great fit for our team. For this specific role, please note that native/fluent French, prior Marketing experience, and English proficiency are mandatory requirements.

      WHAT WE OFFER YOU 

      With thoughtful benefits, emotional wellbeing resources, and a culture that empowers you to take ownership of your role and your wellbeing, we create an environment where you can thrive in all dimensions of your life. Our benefits include:

      WELLHUB:  Free Gold membership with access to onsite gyms and studios, digital fitness programs, and online wellness resources for meditation, nutrition, mental wellbeing support, and more! Add up to three family members to your plan, ensuring access to wellness for those who matter most to you. 

      HEALTHCARE: Health insurance.

      FLEXIBLE WORK: As a Flexible First company, we offer hybrid and remote options to give you the freedom to work in a way that suits you. The model for this specific role can be discussed with your recruiter and hiring manager. We offer all employees a one-time reimbursement to set up their home office equipment and a monthly work allowance to help cover the costs of working from home.

      FLEXIBLE SCHEDULE:  Flexibility for us isn't just about where we work—it also means being able to shape how and when we get things done. Together with their leaders, employees define schedules that align with their time zones, team needs, and personal routines.

      PAID TIME OFF: We know how important it is to take time away from work to recharge. Employees receive a minimum of 25 days paid holiday per year with an additional day for each year of tenure (up to 5) in addition to annual holidays (including an extra holiday on your birthday!).

      PARENTAL LEAVE: Welcoming a new child is one of the most special moments in your life. Take the time to be present and enjoy your growing family. We offer 100% paid parental leave to all new parents. Parents giving birth are eligible for an extended leave and a ramp-back period to return part-time while they get settled.  

      CAREER GROWTH: Access world-class platforms, participate in interactive sessions,  build your personalized development roadmap, and explore internal opportunities. We focus on continuous learning and feedback to support your journey toward personal and professional success. 

      CULTURE: You'll join a team of passionate people who come together to break boundaries, support each other, and create a meaningful impact in workplace wellness. We win together, building trust through open communication and a culture where every perspective matters. Learn more about our shared culture and values here. 

      And to get a glimpse of life at Wellhub… Follow us on Instagram @lifeatwellhub and LinkedIn!

      Who We Are

      Hi, we're DuckDuckGo, the online protection company and remote-first team of 300+ on a mission to raise the standard of trust online. Founded in 2008 and profitable since 2014, annual revenue now exceeds $100m USD and millions use our browser on on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android, our search engine, and the DuckDuckGo subscription. We also offer private, useful, and optional AI, including Duck.ai, which lets you chat privately with ChatGPT, Claude, and other AIs, all in one place. Our culture of trust, inclusivity, and empowered project management underpins everything we do, where each team member takes full ownership of their projects, from scoping and execution to postmortem. If you're seeking end-to-end ownership of your work, you've come to the right place!

       

      Your Team and Role

      As a Senior Product Designer, Design Systems you'll be the first of its kind at DuckDuckGo. You'll take ownership of our design system at a pivotal moment, with a chance to define both a role and a roadmap from the ground up — helping build the process, not just step into one. You'll audit our existing system, lead projects that move it forward across platforms and products like Duck.ai and Search, as well as shape how we manage and scale it as we grow.

       

      Applying your hands-on design skills, you will autonomously lead highly impactful projects that scale across millions of users, and collaborate with team members at all levels to pioneer new solutions as we build out the privacy layer for the internet. From ideation to execution, you'll assess vague problems, propose high-impact solutions, and execute them against a set of success criteria. You'll have a voice in all product-related design decisions, whether large or small, and an opportunity to work on a team dedicated to our ethical, privacy by design approach. Read more about Design at DuckDuckGo on our blog: https://spreadprivacy.com/ethical-by-design/

       

      About You

      • 7+ years of experience in product or design systems roles, including 2+ years in senior-level design positions at significant global consumer brands

      Who are we?

      The sea is the physical layer of the economy: our energy, data and trade move across it and under it. It is also Europe's most exposed flank. Cheap underwater drones, divers and mines now threaten ports, naval bases, subsea cables and offshore energy sites, and most of what is funded today stops at detection: it tells you a drone has entered the harbour, not how to stop it before it reaches the hull or the cable.

      Pelagon is creating the category of maritime interdiction: detection and action together. We design, deploy and operate protection zones around critical maritime infrastructure: a persistent sensing network running our own acoustic-first AI detects and classifies threats, and an underwater interceptor acts on them.

      We sell to navies and coast guards, and to the civilian operators of ports, subsea cables and offshore energy.

      Pelagon was founded by Aymeric de Pontbriand (serial deeptech entrepreneur, founded and exited Scortex) and Gauthier Bouxin (French Navy officer, then McKinsey). A team is already in place around them: a lead embedded systems engineer, a lead hardware engineer and an a chief of staff. We are backed by Hexa, the pioneer startup studio in Europe behind Front, Aircall and Spendesk.

      ⚡ What is at stake in the coming months

      • Confirm the technology at sea with navies and operators.

      • Deploy and sign our first paid pilots.

      • Sign our first contracts.

      By joining us, you'll play a key role in turning that early traction into multi-year protection contracts, and in building the sales team that follows.

      🎯 Your mission

      • Own every deal from first meeting to signed contract, with navies, port authorities and operators of cables and offshore energy.

      • Sell interdiction, not detection alone: make the threat and the gap between alarm and response concrete for each buyer, then turn pilots into multi-year protection contracts.

      • Shape requirements before the tender: work with navies and operators months ahead of an RFP so that it asks for detection and action together.

      • Open our priority export markets: the Baltic and the Nordics, the Black Sea, the Gulf and Southeast Asia.

      • Work as a pair with Gauthier, our Co-CEO, on key accounts, and bring Aymeric and the engineers in when the technical conversation starts.

      • Build the partner channel: primes and integrators, offshore and cable operators, and local partners in each country.

      • Turn every deployment into a reference the next customer can check.

      • Set up the sales machine, then hire and lead the first sellers.

      📈 How you will be measured

      • First 3 months: you own the pipeline, have a qualified deal plan for each priority region, and a first paid pilot or LOI is signed.

      • 6 months: paid pilots are running and the first contracts are signed.

      • 12 months: recurring contracts in at least two countries, and your first sales hires are made and ramped.

      🤩 This job is your dream job if:

      • You have closed defense or government deals and want to do it again, from zero, where every contract changes the trajectory

      • You like being the second half of a founder pair: the CEO brings operational credibility, you bring the deal

      • You'd rather be on a plane to Tallinn, Constanța or Abu Dhabi than in a forecast meeting

      • You speak engineer well enough to sell sensors, AI and C2

      • You want to write the sales playbook yourself, then hire the team that runs it

      🙅 This job is not for you if:

      • You need a brand, a marketing team and SDRs to sell

      • You have only sold short-cycle SaaS or SMB deals, never through formal procurement

      • You want to manage a large team from day one rather than close deals yourself

      • Sales cycles of 12 to 24 months and 40% travel put you off

      • You are looking for the comfort of a large defense group

      What we offer

      • A founding role in a seed-stage defense tech company backed by Hexa

      • Fixed salary, variable on signed revenue, BSPCE

      • Offices in Paris, real deployments at sea

      🧭 Our recruitment process

      1. A first call to get to know each other.

      2. A deep dive into two deals you closed.

      3. A case study on a real Pelagon challenge, presented to the founders.

      4. A conversation with the founders.

      5. Reference checks, with your consent.

      6. Offer.

      We answer after each step.

      Pelagon is committed to creating a diverse environment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment irrespective of gender, origin, identity, background and sexual orientation.

      Europe's defense industrial base cannot respond at the speed modern conflict requires. Legacy suppliers operate on month-long timelines. Tribal knowledge is retiring. Supply chains are fragile.       Description

      Legal AI content is turning into a commodity. Every vendor ships the same AI-generated blog posts and the same generic battlecards. We are transitioning into an AI-native company ourselves, and that changes what this role has to be. You would sit in the marketing department with a dotted line to the product department, but not as a traditional product marketer who ships a few blog posts and calls it enablement. Not as a pure thinker who never touches a sales deck. Instead, as one person who owns our voice and turns it into everything the company needs to win: the thesis that gets us cited, the sales slide that closes next week’s deal, and the briefing that gets a General Counsel to say yes.

      You will use AI tooling and agents to cover ground that used to take a small team, so you can spend your own time on the part that cannot be delegated: the thinking, the judgment, and the writing that actually changes someone’s mind.


      Your mission

      1. Product Marketing & Market Intelligence 

      • Drive go-to-market impact for launches and expansion, from plan to execution.

      • Own deep knowledge of our ICP and competitive landscape, and feed it back into the product and sales strategy.

      • Bring market and customer truth back to Product so we build what actually matters.

      • Work across Product, Marketing, Sales and leadership. You don’t sit in a silo.

      2. Positioning, Narrative & Thought Leadership 

      • Own positioning: define what Legartis stands for, against which alternatives, for which buyer.

      • Develop and defend clear, evidence-backed points of view on where Legal AI is going. Not generic AI-created opinions, but real positions based on customer and buyer research (interviews with General Counsel, CFOs, legal operations leaders).

      • Conceive flagship studies and thought leadership content. Direct AI tools to help you scale production while you own the substance and the voice.

      • Own our thought leadership channels, including video, and decide what gets said. Write what can’t be delegated: founder posts, executive bylines, keynote scripts, board-level memos.

      3. Sales & Customer-Facing Enablement 

      • Build the sales slides, briefings, one-pagers and competitive battlecards that make Sales and Customer Success more effective in every conversation.

      • Translate positioning and research into materials for specific deals, verticals and executive-level conversations.

      • Work directly with Sales and CS to find out what’s missing in the field. Build case studies and customer proof points that Sales actually uses, not ones that sit in a folder.

      What We Want to Achieve Together

      In 6 months: a flagship study that gets cited by competitors and customers. Sales armed with materials that actually get used in deals. A clear Legartis position that everyone in the company can repeat in 30 seconds.

      In 12 months: Legartis recognized as one of the leading European voices on Legal AI, with a content and enablement engine, you plus the AI tools you direct, that outproduces companies with five times the headcount.


      Your profile

      • Proven strategist: demonstrated success creating and executing marketing strategies.

      • Storyteller: you craft compelling materials about complex AI products for non-technical audiences.

      • Clear communicator: exceptional written and verbal communication with a strong visual sensibility.

      • Impact-driven: comfortable with experimentation and interpreting both quantitative and qualitative data.

      • AI-savvy: crafty with AI tools and automations — you use them daily and keep exploring what's new.

      • A track record where writing and thinking were central: journalism, industry or analyst research, strategy consulting, or senior product marketing with real strategic ownership. 4+ years in marketing, product marketing or a comparable strategic role at a SaaS company. Classic PMM experience (positioning, GTM, enablement) is a strong plus, not a hard requirement, if your thinking and writing are strong enough.

      • Fluent German and English, executive-level writing in both.


      Why us?

      • Real editorial ownership over our voice and our position, not a content calendar handed down from someone else.

      • A platform to build your own visible profile as a voice in Legal AI.

      • Modern office in Leipzig or Berlin, hybrid setup, with regular presence in Zürich and team events such as hiking, dinners and offsites.

      • Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) participation.

      • Competitive salary, based on experience and seniority.


      Process

      1. 30 min with our People & Operations Manager: cultural fit, understanding the role and your expectations.

      2. Positioning conversation with our Head of Product: bring a point of view on Legal AI and be ready to defend it live.

      3. Case study: show us something you’ve written or built, and how you’d turn it into a sales-ready asset.

      4. Meet the team in the office.

      5. Decision: if it’s mutual, we welcome you to the team!

      How to Apply

      Send us your CV, two or three writing or work samples you’re proud of, and a short note answering: what’s your sharpest point of view on where Legal AI is heading, and what’s the evidence?

      Gravis Robotics is a high-growth Series A start-up backed by SoftBank, bringing Physical AI to the construction industry, turning heavy construction machines into autonomous robots.

We're looking for a senior IC to own the analog power chain end-to-end across our UXV platforms: from MOSFET commutation simulation through PCB layout to lab validation.       • Power Stage Architecture: Lead motor-controller and DC-DC topology across fixed-wing, multicopter, and hybrid UXV platforms. Translate mission constraints into power-chain specification.

      Network Operations Engineer

      1. About the role

      Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure into a single layer and give ISPs, hyperscalers, and AI companies a clean path to deliver connectivity into every home and business across Kenya and the continent. Behind that marketplace is a real network: a BGP edge peering with Tier 1 transit, hyperscalers, and local exchanges, an MPLS backbone, aggregation and access gear, and the systems that watch all of it.

      For the partners who run on us, the network is the product, and the NOC is where they feel it. A clean shift is a partner who never knew anything happened. That is the bar.

      We are early and the team is small, so we cannot afford a pair of hands that only knows how to escalate. We need a capable network engineer who can stand a shift, resolve real faults without waking anyone, and then keep building the network while East Africa sleeps: propagation and peering checks, health passes across the estate, config changes through to merge, tickets off the board, automation that takes the next repetitive job off everyone's plate. The watching is the floor of this role, not the ceiling.

      The NOC you would be joining is not a legacy one. We are building it as an AI assisted operations environment from the ground up. The forwarding plane runs on open source routing and forwarding software, every device configuration lives in Git, and an LLM layer sits on top of the live network state. When something moves, that layer reads the telemetry, correlates it against the topology and the config history, and puts a probable cause and a candidate fix in front of the engineer on shift. The point is not to replace your judgment. It is to collapse the time between an alert firing and you knowing where to look, so mean time to repair is measured in minutes.

      You sit inside that system. You use it, you push back on it when it is wrong, and what you catch that it misses is part of how it gets smarter. As we build automation out across the NOC, you are not just a consumer of the tooling. You help write it.

      2. What you'll do

      Watch, and know what you're looking at. Sit on our monitoring stack (Zabbix and Grafana dashboards, flow telemetry, alerting) and actually read it. Learn what normal looks like so abnormal jumps out at you: a BGP session that dropped, a link that went down, latency climbing on a path, a capacity threshold breached, a partner suddenly pushing or pulling nothing.

      Troubleshoot and resolve. This is where you earn your seat. Confirm the alert is real, gather the facts, and localise the fault: one peer or many, us or upstream, a real outage or a monitoring blip. The assistive layer surfaces a likely diagnosis and a suggested fix, the config history is right there in Git, and the runbooks are live. Your job is to read all of it critically, decide what is actually true, and close out what you can on your own. Every ticket you resolve yourself is one our senior people did not get pulled out of deep work, or out of bed, to deal with.

      Keep the network healthy, not just alive. A quiet shift is not an idle one. Run the proactive passes: check that routes are propagating the way they should, that RPKI and filter chains are doing their job, that peering and transit sessions are clean across the edge, that no PoP is drifting toward a capacity wall. Catch the slow degradations that never trip an alert. The day team should inherit a network in a known good state.

      Build and automate. The repetitive parts of this job should not stay repetitive. Write the scripts that turn a manual check into a scheduled one. Push our config automation forward (Jinja driven generation, NAPALM or NETCONF/gNMI against the devices) so changes ship from data, not from memory. When the assistive layer keeps missing the same thing, that is a candidate for automation, and you are well placed to build it during the hours nobody else is online.

      Move the work forward. You are part of the network team, working the same board they do. Pick up tickets from the Linear queue, take config changes through review to merge, and keep our source of truth (Nautobot) accurate as the estate changes. Real work lands while East Africa is offline, so the team wakes up further ahead than they went to bed.

      Report exactly what is happening. For everything you cannot or should not fix alone, the handoff has to be clean: what is wrong, where, since when, what is affected, whether it is getting worse, and what you have already tried. No guessing dressed up as fact. No "the internet is down." A clear, written incident note a senior engineer can act on the moment they open it, and a tidy handover to the East Africa team at the end of your shift.

      Escalate well. Know the ladder cold: what you are cleared to touch, what you must not touch alone, and who to bring in for what. Escalating early on a genuine outage is good judgment. Sitting silently on a problem because you were unsure is the one thing that gets people out of bed angry. Handle what you can, raise the rest fast and clearly, and do not turn either dial too far.

      3. Who we're looking for

      A network engineer who can stand on their own through a shift, and who treats the quiet hours as time to build rather than time to wait. You will not be the most senior engineer on this team, and you do not need to be. The people you escalate to are CCIE level. What we need from you is independence and range: work a problem properly, resolve a fair share of it yourself, and use what is left of the shift to actually move the network forward. Pair that with clear reporting, sound judgment about when to bring in help, and the instinct to question a machine's suggestion rather than follow it blindly, and you are who we are looking for.

      Must-have

      • Strong networking competence, held in your hands rather than on paper. CCNA and well beyond it. You understand TCP/IP, routing and switching, IP addressing and subnetting, DNS, DHCP, NAT, and how they behave when they go wrong.

      • Real troubleshooting instinct. Given a degraded link or a dropped session, you know where to look and what to rule out. You can read BGP session state, follow a path with ping and traceroute, and tell a local fault from an upstream one without waiting to be told.

      • Working BGP knowledge. Reading communities and route policy, spotting a flap or a leaky origin, understanding how transit, peering, and RPKI behave at the edge.

      • Comfortable on the gear and the CLI. Linux, network device CLIs, and dashboards are familiar ground. We run MikroTik (RouterOS) across the network and so do many partners, so RouterOS experience is a real plus.

      • Comfortable working with config in Git. Configuration lives in repos, not on devices. Reading a diff, understanding why a config changed, and proposing one yourself should not be foreign to you.

      • Some scripting, and the appetite to do more. Bash or Python, enough to automate the repetitive parts away and to grow into our config and automation pipelines. We are not hiring a button pusher.

      • Clear written English. You can describe a technical situation accurately and briefly so someone picking it up cold understands it instantly.

      • Calm under pressure and dependable. When the graphs go red you get more precise, not more panicked. You show up for every shift, alert and on time.

      • Located in New Zealand or a nearby time zone where covering our deep overnight maps onto your normal working day.

      Nice-to-have

      • Working familiarity with FreeRADIUS, CoA and Disconnect flows, and how session control and accounting hook into the network.

      • Exposure to applying ML or AI in network operations: anomaly detection, predictive failure analysis, automated triage or remediation.
